anil-wadhwa: Anil Wadhwa is Former Secretary (East) Ministry of External Affairs and Ambassador to Italy, Oman, Poland, and Thailand.Top of FormBottom of Form
bhuchung-d-sonam: Bhuchung D Sonam is an exiled Tibetan writer, translator, and publisher whose works explore contemporary Tibetan literature, identity, politics, music, and culture. His notable books include: Songs from Dewachen and Yak Horns: Notes on Contemporary Tibetan Writing, Music, Film and Politics. He is a founding member of TibetWrites and its publishing imprint, Blackneck Books. His essays, commentaries, and literary writings have appeared in prominent international publications including the Washington Post, Asahi Weekly, the Journal of Indian Literature, and HIMAL Southasian, among others.

biswas-baral: ** Biswas Baral is the Editor of The Kathmandu Post and a columnist for The Diplomat. With two decades of experience in Nepali journalism, he previously served as the editor-in-chief of The Annapurna Express, a national news weekly, and is host of the popular YouTube show 'Idea of Nepal'. He mostly writes on Nepal's domestic politics and its foreign policy. Baral holds a Master's Degree in Political Science from the Tribhuvan University and an Executive MBA from the Ace Institute of Management.
claude-arpi: Claude Arpi is a French-born author, journalist, and Tibetologist born in 1949 in Angoulême, France, who has lived in India for nearly five decades and is an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI). He currently serves as a Distinguished Fellow at the Centre of Excellence for Himalayan Studies, Shiv Nadar Institution of Eminence, Delhi. He is the author of numerous books and articles on Tibet, China, India, and Indo-French relations, including the widely regarded The Fate of Tibet: When Big Insects Eat Small Insects. He also held the prestigious Field Marshal K.M. Cariappa Chair of Excellence at the United Service Institution of India (USI), where he conducted extensive research on the Indian presence in Tibet between 1947 and 1962, later published in four volumes by Vij Books India. Claude Arpi who lives in Auroville, serves as the Director of the Pavilion of Tibetan Culture. The Pavilion was inaugurated by Tenzin Gyatso on 20 January 2009 in the presence of Claude Arpi.
dilip-sinha: Dilip Sinha, a former diplomat, is now a writer and public speaker. He was India's ambassador to the United Nations in Geneva and to Greece, and head of the International Organisations and the Pakistan-Afghanistan-Iran divisions in the Ministry of External Affairs. He has authored two books: (i) Imperial Games in Tibet: The Struggle for Statehood and Sovereignty, and (ii) Legitimacy of Power: The Permanence of Five in the Security Council. 1: Jawaharlal Nehru, 'Statement in Parliament on 4 September 1959', in India's Foreign Policy, New Delhi, Publications Division, Government of India, 1961, p. 344.
dolkun-isa: Dolkun Isa is a co-founder and former leader of the World Uyghur Congress. He currently serves as President of the Uyghur Center for Democracy and Human Rights and holds positions on both the Asia Freedom Institute Advisory Board and the UNPO Presidency. Isa began his career as a student leader at Xinjiang University but was expelled due to his activism, after which he sought asylum in Germany in 1994. Internationally recognised for his advocacy on Uyghur human rights, Isa is the author of China Freedom Trap: My Life on the Run, and has been honoured with several awards, including the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation Award (2016), the NED World Democracy Award (2019), and honorary membership in the German Society for Threatened Peoples (2023).
enghebatu-togochog: Born in Southern Mongolia, Enghebatu Togochog came to the United States in 1998. In 2001, he established the Southern Mongolian Human Rights Information Center (SMHRIC), New York. Currently he is the Director of the SMRHIC and the chief editor of the organisational newsletter "Southern Mongolia Watch". He has testified on human rights conditions of Southern Mongolia before the US Congressional Executive Commission on China, United Nations Human Rights Council, United Nations Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues, United Nations Forum on Minority Issues, United Nations Committee Against Torture, and European Parliament. His work include the translation of "Way Out of Southern Mongolia" and "Genocide on the Mongolian Steppe" (Volume I and Volume II). ———————————————————————– ———————————————————————–
gabriel-lafitte: Gabriel Lafitte is editor at rukor.org, which since 2011 has published 200,000 words of analytic insights into contemporary Tibet. He has spent years living with Tibetans, in exile and in Tibet. Based in Australia, he researches the impacts of Chinese policies on the Tibetan Plateau, and regularly trains young Tibetan professional environmentalists and advocates. Decades of immersion in Tibetan culture, and a dozen journeys around China, have given him an insider/outsider perspective on two great civilisations in conflict. He is an experienced public policy adviser with expertise in development, biodiversity, and resource management policy. He has authored numerous reports, submissions, and a 2006 book on the Dalai Lama's teachings Happiness in a Material World. 1: Rong, Zhou (2019). gyal-lo: Gyal Lo (Jia Luo), a prolific author, received his PhD from the University of Toronto and was awarded Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRCC) Fellowship for his research titled "Culturally Relevant Education for Minority and Rural Village in Asia." He has taught for over a decade as a faculty member at the Department of Tibetan Language and Culture, the Northwest University for Nationalities. Currently, he was appointed as a Tibet Specialist at Tibet Action Institute. His research interests cover Educational Sociology; the Structuration Theory, Tibetan Buddhism in Society, Mother Tongue and its Policy, Indigenous Knowledge in Curriculum, Social-Cultural Reproduction, Sociological Studies of Spirituality, and Multilingualism.
hon-shiang-lau: Hon-Shiang LAU is an eminent Chinese scholar and was Chair Professor at the City University of Hong Kong. He retired in 2012 to concentrate on his research on China-Tibet historical relationship. Prof LAU received his Ph.D. from University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, USA, in 1973. He was: Regents Professor, Oklahoma State University, USA, 1987-2000; Chair Professor of Operations Management, City University of Hong Kong, 2000-2012; and was appointed 'Consulting Professor' by PRC's Shanghai Jiaotong University (1981) and Shanghai Tongji University (1985).
jampa-samten: Jampa Samten is a retired Professor, teaching History of Indian and Tibetan Buddhism and Tibetan History at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (Deemed University), Varanasi, India. His main field of study is Tibetan Buddhism. He completed his Doctor's Dissertation on "The Critical Study of Samvarodaya Tantra and Commentary by Indian scholar Ratnarakshita" of the 12th century, from Visva Bharati University, Shantinikitan, India. His publications include over 30 research papers and 10 books (including co-authored books) that include "A Catalogue of the Phug Manuscript Kanjur" LTWA, Dharamsala, 1992 and "From Tibet Confidentially: Secret Correspondence of the Thirteenth Dalai Lama to Agvan Dorzhiev," 1911-1925, LTWA, Dharamsala, 2012. The survey and study of the history of Canonical Buddhist literatures translated and preserved in Tibetan language has been his main area of research. Jampa is currently working on a book entitled "Bod kyi bKa' 'gyur dang bsTan 'gyur gyi byung rim lo rgyus (A History of Tibetan Tripitaka)" and the editing of a Sanskrit and Tibetan Text of Samvarodaya Tantra with content summary in English. Another book on the subject, written together with Hiroaki Niisaku, rGyal rtse Them spangs ma'i bKa' 'gyur dkar chag: A Catalogue of the Ulan Bator rGyal rtse Them spangs ma Manuscript Kangyur, is scheduled to be published by Tokyo: Sankibo (2013) in press. 1: Kanjur meaning "the Translations of the Buddhavachan" (Buddha's teachings). This collection consists of 100 volumes. 2: Tanjur meaning "the Translations of the treatises (śāstra)" authored by Indian scholars of 1st to 12th century. This collection consists of 225 volumes.
jyotsna-roy: Jyotsna Roy is a social scientist with over four decades of experience in institutional and social development, mostly in post-conflict countries in Southeast Asia, South Asia, and East and Southern Africa, serving as a team leader and expert with multilateral and bilateral organisations.\ As an advocate for the Tibet cause, she is currently the National Treasurer of the India Tibet Friendship Society (ITFS). Jyotsna has been a member of the "Organising Committee for the Tenshug Offering, 2026", and served as editor of the commemorative souvenir. Ritual as action here refers to understanding ritual not just as symbolic or devotional expression, but as a practice that produces social and political effects. It becomes a way through which collective identity is affirmed, ethical commitments are expressed, and continuity is sustained, especially where formal institutional or diplomatic avenues are limited. Embodied presence refers to people being physically present together in a shared space, where meaning, commitment, and social relations are expressed through participation. It highlights that engagement is not only symbolic but also involves being visibly and collectively present.

kelsang-gyaltsen: Kelsang Gyaltsen is currently serving in a honorary capacity as Co-Vice President of the Gaden Phodrang Foundation of the Dalai Lama in Zurich and as a senior advisor to the Tibetan Government-in-Exile. He worked for over 30 years in the service of the Dalai Lama as his representative in Europe, as the private secretary for international relations at the Office of HH the Dalai Lama, Dharamsala, India, and as his envoy for talks with Beijing. In this role, he and his senior colleague, Lodi Gyari, led the Tibetan negotiating team in talks between the Tibetan and Chinese leadership from 2002 to 2010.

ming-xia: Ming Xia is a Professor of Political Science at the Department of Political Science and Global Affairs, the College of Staten Island, the City University of New York and a doctoral faculty member at the CUNY Graduate Center. He received his degrees from Fudan University and Temple University. He once taught at Fudan University and served as a residential fellow at the Sigur Center for Asian Studies, George Washington University (2003), the Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars (2004), the East Asian Institute at the National University of Singapore (2004 and 2011), and the Asian Research Institute at NUS (2012).

srikanth-kondapalli: Srikanth Kondapalli is Professor in Chinese Studies at the Centre for East Asian Studies, School of International Studies, Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), New Delhi. He was former Dean of School of International Studies, JNU from 2022-24; Chairman of the Centre for East Asian Studies, SIS, JNU from 2008-10, 2012-20, and in 2022. He is Chair Professor under the Chair of Excellence of Ministry of Defence since August 2022. He is a distinguished fellow at several think-tanks including Vivekananda International Foundation and Institute for Peace and Conflict Studies. He has supervised more than 30 Ph.D. researchers at JNU and is also an academic advisor for Ph.D. researchers at Al Farabi Kazakh National University and Ablai Khan University at Almaty and Tamkhang University (Taipei). He is a Trustee with the Foundation for Non-violent Alternatives (FNVA) since 2021.
sriparna-pathak: Sriparna Pathak is a Professor of China Studies, and the founding Director of the Centre for Northeast Asian Studies at O.P. Jindal Global University, (JGU) Haryana, India. She also serves in the capacity of a Senior Fellow, at the Jindal India Institute, and is also an Associate Director at the Motwani Jadeja Institute of American Studies at JGU. Dr. Pathak is also associated with Taiwan's Doublethink Lab, as a regional partner, and works on tracking China's influence operations.
tenzin-dalha: Tenzin Dalha is a Research Fellow at the Tibet Policy Institute, Central Tibetan Administration, where he researches the impact of social media on Tibetan communities in Tibet and exile, as well as Chinese cyber security policy. He received his M.Phil. in Journalism and Communication from the University of Madras in 2014. He has presented at institutions including Johns Hopkins University and the University of Westminster, and has contributed commentaries to The Diplomat and Global-is-Asian. Prior to joining TPI, he worked as a freelance journalist and documentary contributor.
tenzin-lamsang: Tenzing Lamsang is the founder and editor of The Bhutanese newspaper. He is an award winning journalist from Bhutan and brings a wealth of critical perspectives and a deeper understanding of the daily issues affecting the nation. He is best known for his daring investigative journalism. tenzin-thinley: Tenzin Thinley serves as the Fundraising Officer and Operations Lead at Monlam Charitable Trust, where he works to advance the preservation and promotion of Tibetan language and culture through innovative technological initiatives. He leads fundraising efforts, cultivates strategic partnerships, and oversees the Trust's daily operations. Among his notable contributions is the Tibetan Digital Library Project, a major initiative dedicated to safeguarding Tibet's literary and cultural heritage in digital form for future generations. His interests in artificial intelligence, politics, and international relations reflect a wider engagement with the impact of technology on society and global affairs. Thinley studied at TCV schools, UWC Atlantic College, and Methodist University.
